title: 12 Best Places to Hire AI Developers (2026)

blocks.text: 12 Best Places to Hire AI Developers (2026)

Hiring an AI developer in 2026 means choosing between vetted freelance marketplaces, AI talent networks, nearshore staffing companies, open marketplaces, job boards or a placement service. This guide compares the 12 best places to hire AI developers, with the vetting, fees and timelines each company publishes on its own site.

Hiring an AI developer in 2026 means choosing between five different models: a vetted freelance marketplace (Toptal, Arc.dev, Lemon.io), an AI-focused talent network (Turing, Andela), a nearshore staffing company (BairesDev), an open marketplace or job board where you do the screening (Upwork, Gun.io, Braintrust, Wellfound, Hacker News), or a placement service that sources, vets and backs the hire for you. This guide compares the 12 best places to hire AI developers in 2026, with the vetting, fees and timelines each company publishes on its own site, plus a framework for matching the hiring model to how urgently and how long you need the engineer.
Best places to hire AI developers: a brief overview

ManasFlow (Engineer Placement): Best for an agent-trained AI engineer placed fast, from our own bench in 2 to 4 weeks, from $60,000 a year, with a 90-day replacement guarantee. It is our own service, disclosed below. For a multi-role team instead of one placement, see our dedicated AI developers offer.
Toptal: Best for premium vetted freelance AI talent. Toptal says about 3% of applicants pass its screening, and every engagement starts with a trial of up to two weeks.
Turing: Best for AI-lab-grade experts. Turing says it screens with human and AI evaluation and onboards talent in days.
Arc.dev: Best for published rates. Freelance hires run $15 to $110+ per hour, and full-time hires cost 20% of annual salary.
Lemon.io: Best for startups that want a vetted freelancer matched in about a day. Lemon.io says 1.2% of applicants are accepted.
Andela: Best for AI engineering teams from a global network across 135+ countries, including AI-trained engineers.
BairesDev: Best for a nearshore AI team in North American time zones, as staff augmentation, a dedicated team or a full outsourced project.
Upwork: Best for short, well-scoped AI tasks where you screen candidates yourself.
Gun.io: Best for a curated shortlist with contracts, payroll and compliance handled for you.
Braintrust: Best for zero talent-side fees plus an AI recruiter (AIR) for high-volume screening.
Wellfound: Best job board for startups hiring full-time AI engineers, with free unlimited job posts.
Hacker News "Who is hiring?": Best free community channel for reaching senior engineers once a month.
1. ManasFlow, best for an agent-trained AI engineer placed fast

Our five published case studies show the kind of systems our engineers ship.

Placement takes 2 to 4 weeks from request to start, starts from $60,000 a year with no recruitment fee, and every placement comes with a 90-day replacement guarantee: if the fit is wrong, we replace the engineer at no extra cost. If you want a product built rather than a person placed, we also run a fixed-price 30-day SaaS MVP sprint.
Key features
Engineers sourced from our own bench, trained on AI agent orchestration, not a generic staffing pool.
2 to 4 week placement timeline.
90-day replacement guarantee.
No recruitment fee on top of the placement price.
Best for
Teams that want an AI-agent-capable engineer embedded on their team, not an agency project.
Companies that have tried general dev-marketplace hires and found the AI-specific skill gap too wide.
Pricing
Placement from $60,000 a year, no recruitment fee.
Fixed-price 30-day SaaS MVP sprint if you want a product delivered instead.
Pros
A fixed start window (2 to 4 weeks), with a guarantee if the fit is wrong.
Engineers already fluent in modern AI agent tooling, not learning it on your dime.
Direct relationship, with no marketplace platform fee layered between you and the engineer.
Cons
Smaller bench than a large open marketplace like Upwork or a network like Andela, so availability depends on current placements.
Not a self-serve platform; every placement starts with a scoping conversation.

2. Toptal, best for premium vetted freelance AI talent

Toptal is an exclusive freelance network that lists AI engineers, AI developers and AI researchers among its hiring categories. Its FAQ says fewer than 3% of applicants pass a screening that includes portfolio reviews, technical coding challenges and live problem-solving sessions. Toptal says its average time to match is under 24 hours, and each engagement starts with a trial of up to two weeks: if you are not satisfied, you are not billed.
Key features
Screening with coding challenges and live problem-solving; Toptal says about 3% of applicants pass.
Hourly, part-time or full-time engagements at a fixed weekly price.
Trial period of up to two weeks, billed only if you are satisfied.
Best for
Business-critical hires where vetting quality matters more than price.
Short-term or flexible engagements that need a vetted freelancer fast.
Pricing
A flat $79 monthly subscription fee if you proceed with talent matching.
Talent rates are not published; Toptal quotes a fixed weekly price per engagement.
Pros
Published, specific screening steps rather than a vague "vetted" label.
Flexible engagement length (hourly through full-time).
Trial period lowers the cost of a wrong match.
Cons
No published rate card, so you only see the real price after matching.
The monthly subscription fee sits on top of the talent's rate.
3. Turing, best for AI-lab-grade experts

Turing now leads its site with two businesses: helping frontier AI labs improve models with data and expertise, and helping enterprises deploy agentic systems. Its talent page offers engineers, full-stack developers and product leaders it describes as trusted by leading AI labs. Turing says every expert goes through human and AI evaluation (technical challenges, peer interviews and its own AI models), claims a 5M+ expert pool and says talent is onboarded in days.
Key features
Human + AI evaluation: technical challenges, peer interviews and proprietary model scoring.
5M+ expert pool across 250+ domains (Turing's own figures).
Onboarding in days, according to Turing.
A separate enterprise track for deploying agentic systems.
Best for
Companies that want engineers with experience close to AI model work (evaluation, data, agentic systems).
Enterprises that may want an AI delivery partner as well as individual experts.
Pricing
Not published. You describe the role in a contact form and Turing surfaces a matched set of experts.
Pros
Talent pool built around AI lab work rather than general web development.
Fast onboarding, per Turing's own claim.
Can scale from one expert to an enterprise deployment.
Cons
No public pricing; every engagement starts with a form and a sales conversation.
Talent hiring is one line of business next to AI lab data work, so confirm which service you are buying.
4. Arc.dev, best for published freelance and full-time rates

Arc.dev combines vetting with AI-assisted screening and sourcing, and it publishes its prices. Freelance hires run $15 to $110+ per hour with a risk-free trial of up to two weeks, and full-time hires cost 20% of the annual salary. Arc says it gives access to 450,000 talent in 190 countries, describes them as the "top 2%", and says you can hire in 72 hours for freelance or 14 days for full-time. You pay $0 until you hire.
Key features
AI applicant screening and auto sourcing on top of human vetting.
Both freelance and full-time hiring paths, with payments and compliance handled.
Risk-free trial of up to two weeks on freelance hires.
Best for
Companies that want to see the price before they start.
Budget-flexible hiring across a wide seniority and rate range.
Pricing
Freelance: $15 to $110+ per hour.
Full-time: 20% of annual salary as a placement fee. $0 until you hire.
Pros
Published pricing for both freelance and full-time hires.
Stated timelines (72 hours freelance, 14 days full-time).
Supports both freelance and full-time engagement models.
Cons
The wide rate range means you still need to check seniority and AI project history yourself.
A 20% placement fee is a real cost on a senior full-time salary.
5. Lemon.io, best for startups that want a vetted freelancer in about a day

Lemon.io is a vetted freelance marketplace built for startups, with AI engineers and AI developers listed among its hiring categories across 50+ technologies. You describe what you need, Lemon.io sources and vets candidates, and you interview pre-qualified engineers; it says most hires happen after 1 to 2 interviews. Lemon.io states a 1.2% acceptance rate and a matching time of about 24 hours. It charges no upfront fees: you pay for work delivered, with no minimum hours or project length.
Key features
Vetting with a stated 1.2% acceptance rate (Lemon.io's own figure).
Matching in about 24 hours, per Lemon.io.
Contract and in-house hiring options.
You own all intellectual property produced for your project.
Best for
Startups that need one or two vetted AI developers quickly.
Teams that want freelance flexibility with no minimum engagement.
Pricing
No upfront fees; you pay only for work delivered.
Hourly rates are not listed on the pricing page; Lemon.io offers a rate calculator and a clear estimate before work begins.
Pros
Short path to a shortlist (about 24 hours, 1 to 2 interviews).
No minimum hours or duration.
Clear IP ownership terms.
Cons
No published hourly rate card; you get the number from the calculator or an estimate.
Built around individual freelancers for startups, so it is a weaker fit if you need a managed team.
Skip it if you need a multi-person team run by a delivery lead; a staffing company like BairesDev or a network like Andela fits that better.
6. Andela, best for AI engineering teams from a global network

Andela is a global tech talent company founded in May 2014, with talent across 135+ countries. It now centers its offer on AI: you can hire engineers trained to build modern AI systems, deploy blended teams (AI application, systems and platform engineers), or buy AI system development and training for your own staff. Andela says it has 17,000 AI-native engineers in its network and trains talent through learning partnerships with Google, NVIDIA, AWS, Microsoft Azure and Meta.
Key features
Talent across 135+ countries (Andela's figure).
Blended AI teams: builders, integrators and scalers.
Training as a Service to upskill your own engineers for AI.
Best for
Enterprises building a distributed AI engineering team rather than a single hire.
Companies that want hiring and AI upskilling from one vendor.
Pricing
Not published. Andela's pricing page routes you to a discovery call.
Pros
Global talent pool across 135+ countries.
Team model suits companies that need several engineers, not just one.
Long operating history (founded 2014).
Cons
No published pricing; every engagement starts with a discovery call.
Built around team and enterprise engagements, so a one-off short task is a weak fit.
7. BairesDev, best for a nearshore AI team in North American time zones

BairesDev is a nearshore software development and staff augmentation company operating since 2009. It offers three models: staff augmentation (individual developers who join your team and work your hours), dedicated teams with BairesDev project management, and full software outsourcing from planning to deployment. It says it has 4,000+ engineers across 100+ technologies, has worked with 500+ companies, and hires what it calls the "top 1%" of talent. AI development, machine learning, LLM applications and generative AI are listed services.
Key features
Three engagement models: staff augmentation, dedicated teams, software outsourcing.
Nearshore teams aligned with North American time zones.
AI and machine learning development, including LLM applications.
Best for
North American companies that want AI engineers working their hours.
Teams that may start with one engineer and grow into a managed team.
Pricing
Not published. BairesDev asks you to schedule a call.
Pros
Can take full ownership of a project, not just supply people.
Time zone overlap with US and Canadian teams.
Long operating history (since 2009).
Cons
No public pricing, so comparing it with published-rate platforms takes a sales call.
Built for company-scale engagements; overkill for a single small task.
Skip it if you need one freelancer for a week-long job; Upwork or Lemon.io is faster to set up. For more on this model, see our guide to nearshore AI developers.
8. Upwork, best for short, well-scoped AI tasks

Upwork is an open freelance marketplace: you post a job, freelancers send proposals, and you review profiles, portfolios and past-job feedback yourself. That makes it a good tool for a narrow, well-defined AI task (a script, a small integration, a proof of concept) where you can judge the deliverable, and a riskier one for an ongoing engineering hire where your own screening has to carry the whole decision.
Key features
Open marketplace where you screen candidates directly.
Hourly and fixed-price project structures.
Profiles show portfolios and past-job feedback.
Best for
Short, well-scoped AI tasks where you can clearly evaluate the deliverable.
Budget-conscious hiring where you are willing to do your own vetting.
Pricing
Rates are set by each freelancer and negotiated per job. Check Upwork's client pricing page for its current marketplace fees.
Pros
Proposals come to you, so you can compare several candidates on one job.
Fixed-price contracts suit well-defined deliverables.
You can start quickly on a small job.
Cons
Screening is on you, so quality depends on how well you interview.
Weak fit for an ongoing embedded engineering hire versus a discrete task.
9. Gun.io, best for a curated shortlist with contracts handled

Gun.io gives you what it calls a high-precision shortlist of vetted developers matched to your stack and delivery goals, drawn from thousands of vetted software professionals worldwide. It also handles negotiations, contracts and onboarding, runs multi-currency payroll and tax compliance across 100+ countries, and tracks milestones and performance after the hire.
Key features
